title: 7.1 Chemical equilibria: reversible reactions, dynamic equilibrium

q.Q1: Q1. Air is about four-fifths nitrogen and one-fifth oxygen by moles, at a total pressure of 100 kPa. What share of the pressure would you expect each gas to provide, and why?
q.Table: Q2. A mixture contains 1.0 mol of N₂ and 3.0 mol of H₂ at a total pressure of 400 kPa.

q.Q3: Q3. At equilibrium in N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), the partial pressure of N₂O₄ is 60 kPa and that of NO₂ is 40 kPa. Calculate Kp, with units.
q.Q4: Q4. An equilibrium mixture of 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g) contains 0.20 mol SO₂, 0.10 mol O₂ and 0.70 mol SO₃ at a total pressure of 200 kPa. Calculate the partial pressure of each gas and then Kp.

q.Table: Q5. Choose the condition used in the Haber process.
q.Q6: Q6. Explain why a temperature of about 450 °C is described as a compromise in the Haber process.

q.Table: Q7. Haber process, Contact process, or both?
q.Q8: Q8. Explain why the Contact process does not use a high pressure, although a high pressure would move the position of equilibrium to the right.

q.Q9: Q9. In the Haber process an equilibrium mixture at a total pressure of 200 atm contains 2.0 mol N₂, 6.0 mol H₂ and 2.0 mol NH₃. (a) Calculate the mole fraction and the partial pressure of ammonia. (b) Write the expression for Kp (describe it in words or symbols). (c) Explain why a pressure higher than 200 atm is not normally used.
